(1) eConsult - what a pile of doodoos. The nonsense questions bear no relation to one's problem. The practice already knows that I smoke 10 packs of Capstan Full Strength a day. Why do I have to confirm that every time I I use this app? What does this have to do with my ingrowing toenail, my ganglion, or indeed my excessive wind? (ie writing reviews like this).
(2) the phone back system. If your phone isn't free to receive the call back, that's it you're done for! You have to start the whole phone in system over again!

In general, I have found the staff and doctors as good as any. Apart from a tendency to reduce, what a GP might consider unnecessary medications. From my experience I have no complaints about the care I have received with perhaps this one exception, MEDICAL REVIEWS.
By this I mean, GP led general health reviews, medication reviews, mental health reviews (as in the case where one might have been referred back to the care of the GP). In all of these cases I am left with the impression that the GP expects the patient to initiate the review. However, ask a mad man if he's insane and he'll probably say no! So how should this work? I have no idea, but I believe it needs looking into.

The real problem, and this has been touched upon in other reviews, is the under resourcing and the under resourcing of the NHS in general that in turn reflects in the GP's budgets.

Back to GMC then. My reduction of the star score from a perfect 5 is for the reasons given above but I am fearful as to how, what is already an over burdened practice, is going to deal with the demand when the huge apartment development, literally opposite the front doors of the surgery, is going to cope. I doubt that the practice will stop accepting new patients as the temptation to receive the additional patient generated income will prove too tempting.
